title: When fine-tuning helps
goal: Choose among a clearer prompt, current evidence and model adaptation.
case: A college assistant uses the correct format but misses a revised policy.
terms: Change instructions or examples for the task without changing weights.
Supply up-to-date evidence at inference time; useful for changing facts and traceable answers.
Train on examples to change learned behaviour; separate development from final test cases.
Update a small trainable low-rank component instead of all model weights.
steps: Compare provided base, prompted and adapted predictions
Inspect a held-out final set once
Recommend a method for a policy update
example: Base 6/10; prompt 8/10; tuned 9/10 on practice cases.
On fresh cases tuned score is 6/10.
The practice gain alone does not prove better generalization.
misconception: Fine-tuning is the right way to add a policy changed yesterday.
correction: Update the source document and retrieval index; weight adaptation is poor for rapidly changing facts.
change: Change one threshold and note why the final set must remain untouched.
metric: Accuracy with numerator and denominator on separate cases
lab: Analyze a supplied results pack without training a model.
output: Comparison table with recommendation and uncertainty.
